subject: Next steps: PT handback timeline, vuln triage & disclosure policy
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dobson <alex@cloudmed.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: PT handback timeline, vuln triage & disclosure policy

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo today — great to learn more about CloudMed’s ingestion pipelines and the PHI boundary you’ve scoped. Quick recap and suggested next steps from a security/compliance standpoint so your security team can move the vendor review forward: 

- SOC 2: you mentioned SOC 2 Type II in progress with an expected completion in Q4. Can you confirm which controls are still in flight (particularly CC6/CC7 equivalents)?
- GDPR/HIPAA: confirm if the environment handling PHI will be isolated in a dedicated project/region (you indicated yes). We’ll include that in the intake packet.
- Pen test handback: CloudMed asked for an example pen test handback and confirmation of our vulnerability disclosure cadence. Attached are two docs to speed things up: our proposed vuln SLA template and an anonymized pen-test summary example.

Proposed vulnerability SLA (open to negotiation):
- Critical: initial acknowledgement within 24h, mitigation plan within 7 days
- High: mitigation plan within 30 days
- Medium: remediation/mitigation within 90 days

Proposed scan cadence / handback options:
- External pentest: handback report (redacted) + CSV of findings within 7 business days of test closure
- Continuous vulnerability scanning: monthly automated scans with quarterly external tests

Questions for your team:
1) Is the 7-day handback window for an external pen test acceptable?
2) Do you require raw exploit PoCs in the handback or would a summarized technical appendix suffice?
3) Any specific disclosure policy constraints (e.g., must be coordinated via third-party PR counsel, embargo periods)?

Next steps I propose:
- You share the completed vendor questionnaire and any SOC 2 draft sections you can (redactions ok).
- We propose a short MPA addendum covering vuln SLA and non-public handback handling; I’ll loop in Legal if you want to pursue this.

Attachments: redwood-vuln-sla-template.pdf, redwood-pt-handback-example-summary.pdf

Happy to hop on a 15–20 minute follow-up with security if that helps — available Mon/Tue next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Alex Dobson <alex@cloudmed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cloudmed.com
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 18:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: PT handback timeline, vuln triage & disclosure policy

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the templates. Quick answers from our side: 

- SOC 2: still in flight, control testing for change management and access logging completes mid-Oct. We can share the SOC 2 bridge letter and scope doc once it's available.
- PHI boundary: yes, the PHI-handling project is isolated and encrypted-at-rest with customer-specific keys.

Regarding the pen test: the security team prefers a redacted report + CSV of findings (IPs and IOCs redacted) rather than raw PoCs. We do want to see a technical appendix for any critical findings (stack trace + exploit steps) but only under NDA-specific handling.

On the SLA: 7 days for handback is aggressive but acceptable for external tests if we can have a 48h heads-up before report delivery so we can coordinate internal triage. The remediation windows look reasonable; our current baseline (with our ISV partners) is critical=72h, high=30d, medium=90d. Could we align critical to 72h instead of 7 days?

I’m attaching the completed vendor questionnaire we have so far — it’s 80% filled, security@cloudmed.com will finish the rest.

Attachments: CloudMed-Vendor-Questionnaire.xlsx

—Alex
Alex Dobson
Director of Information Security | CloudMed Inc.

Vanessa / Neha —

Thanks for the ping. Quick internal notes and suggested language we can share back: 

1) SLA alignment: we have historically offered two variants depending on customer tier: a standard SLA (Critical=7 days) and an accelerated SLA (Critical=72 hours / High=14 days / Medium=60–90 days) for customers with higher sensitivity or contractual requirements. For CloudMed, given PHI scope, offering the accelerated SLA (Critical=72h) is reasonable and aligns with their expectation. We should document which SLA applies in the MPA addendum.

2) Handback contents: we typically provide: redacted report summary, CSV findings export (no raw PoCs), and a technical appendix for Criticals. The appendix is shared under an NDA and via our secure document portal (ephemeral link that expires after 30 days). We can offer extended access for named security contacts.

3) 48h heads-up: operationally fine. We should includea0a 48-hour notification clause in the MPA to allow customer coordination.

4) Scanning cadence: recommend monthly authenticated scanning for infra + quarterly external pentests. Add an option for on-demand scans tied to major releases.

I attached a redlined vuln SLA template (see attachments) — main edits: explicit critical severity definition, reporting format (CSV columns), and handback delivery windows.

If Legal wants to tighten the appendix access, we can require an additional mutual NDA annex that lists named individuals permitted to see PoCs.

Rishi
VP, Applied ML & Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
